intro: Welcome! In this lesson you train your ears for real situations: announcements at the airport and the station, directions and simple instructions, and short conversations. You don't need every word: read the question first, listen for the key information, and stay calm when you hear a word you don't know.
teachingNotes: This is a listening lesson: most practice is 'press play, then answer'. Build on a1-listening-everyday and teach four habits in plain Indonesian: read the question first and predict the answer type (Which gate? → a number, What time? → a time, Left or right? → a direction, Where are they? → a place); listen for that key word, not every word; don't panic or stop at an unknown word (the key information often comes right after it); listen once for the general idea, then again for the detail. Replaying is normal.

Announcements follow a pattern: Attention, please → what (Flight GA 404 to Bali…, The train to Bandung…; the city comes right after 'to') → the key facts: gate or platform + a number, a time, and news. Teach the news as fixed chunks, not new grammar: 'is now boarding at gate 7', 'leaves from platform 3', 'is delayed by 30 minutes' (by + how long), 'now leaves at 9:15' (the new time), 'is cancelled' (British; American 'canceled'), 'final call'. Flight numbers are said digit by digit and 0 is often 'oh' (GA 404 = 'G A four oh four'). Americans often say 'track' for platform.

Common errors to target: hearing thirteen as thirty or fifteen as fifty (gate 13 vs gate 30, delayed by 15 vs 50 minutes): -teen has the stress at the end, -ty at the start; writing the old time instead of the new one after a delay (the new time comes after 'now'); writing the flight number or the time when the question asks for the gate or platform; mixing 'turn left' (what you do) with 'on the left' (where the place is).

Directions and instructions: imperatives are known from A1. New chunks: 'take the second street on the left' (turn at street number 2: learners often turn at the first one), 'go past the bank' (don't stop or turn), 'opposite' (di seberang; American 'across from'), 'at the end of the street', 'cross the road'. Indonesian traps: 'second' here is kedua, not detik; 'take' in 'take the second street' doesn't mean ambil. Instructions: listen for the order words first / then / after that and for 'don't' (jangan); separate amount from frequency ('one tablet three times a day').

Main point of a conversation: where are they (place words: menu, table → restaurant; ticket, platform → station), what does someone want or what is the problem (listen after 'but', 'sorry', 'I can't'), and what do they decide (often at the end, after 'OK', 'fine', 'great'). A soft English 'no' is 'Sorry, I can't' / 'I'm busy then', usually followed by a new idea: 'What about Saturday?' / 'Is Monday OK?'.

Limits: A1 grammar only (present simple and continuous for now, imperatives, can, there is/are, was/were). No past simple, no will or going to, no present perfect, no comparatives; announcements use the present ('The train leaves at…', 'is now boarding'). Listening texts stay short (2–4 sentences or 3–4 short dialogue lines), slow and clear; prices at most a hundred thousand rupiah.

keyPoints.title: Airport and station announcements
keyPoints.explanation: The key facts come after 'Flight … to …' or 'The train to …': gate or platform + a number, a time, and news (is now boarding, is delayed by, is cancelled). After a delay, the new time comes after 'now'. Flight numbers are said digit by digit; 0 is often 'oh'.

examples.en: Flight GA 404 to Bali is now boarding at gate 7.
examples.id: Penumpang penerbangan GA 404 ke Bali sekarang naik pesawat di gate 7.

examples.en: The train to Surabaya is delayed by 30 minutes. It now leaves at 10:15.
examples.id: Kereta ke Surabaya terlambat 30 menit. Sekarang berangkat pukul 10.15.

examples.en: The bus to Malang is cancelled.

id.title: Pengumuman di bandara dan stasiun
id.explanation: Info kuncinya ada setelah 'Flight … to …' atau 'The train to …': gate atau platform (peron) + nomor, jam, dan kabar (is now boarding, is delayed by, is cancelled). Kalau ada keterlambatan, jam yang baru ada setelah kata 'now'. Nomor penerbangan dibaca satu angka demi satu angka; 0 sering dibaca 'oh'.

keyPoints.title: Directions and simple instructions
keyPoints.explanation: Take the second street on the left = turn left at street number 2, not the first one. Go past = don't stop and don't turn; opposite = across the road from. Instructions start with the verb (Press…, Take…); listen for first, then and don't.

examples.en: Go past the school and take the second street on the left.
examples.id: Lewati sekolahnya, lalu belok kiri di jalan kedua.

examples.en: The ATM is opposite the mosque.
First take a number, then wait here.
examples.id: Ambil nomor antrean dulu, lalu tunggu di sini.

id.title: Petunjuk arah dan instruksi sederhana
id.explanation: Take the second street on the left = belok kiri di jalan nomor 2, bukan yang pertama. Go past = lewati, jangan berhenti dan jangan belok; opposite = di seberang. Instruksi diawali kata kerja (Press…, Take…); dengarkan kata first (pertama/dulu), then (lalu) dan don't (jangan).

keyPoints.title: The main point of a short conversation
keyPoints.explanation: The main point is the most important idea, not every detail. Ask: Where are they? What does someone want, or what is the problem? What do they decide? Listen after but, sorry and I can't, and listen to the end: the decision often comes last.

examples.en: Sorry, I can't. I'm busy on Monday. What about Tuesday?
examples.id: Maaf, aku tidak bisa. Aku sibuk hari Senin. Bagaimana kalau hari Selasa?

id.title: Poin utama percakapan pendek
id.explanation: Poin utama (inti) adalah ide yang paling penting, bukan setiap detail. Tanyakan: Mereka di mana? Apa yang diinginkan seseorang, atau apa masalahnya? Apa keputusan mereka? Dengarkan setelah kata but, sorry dan I can't, dan dengarkan sampai akhir: keputusannya sering ada di bagian terakhir.

guidedPractice.prompt: You hear: 'Flight J T two oh five to Lombok is now boarding.' Write the flight number, like GA 123.
guidedPractice.hint: Flight numbers are said one digit at a time, and 'oh' = 0.

guidedPractice.prompt: You hear: 'The train to Yogyakarta is cancelled.' Does the train go today? Write yes or no.
You hear: 'Take the second street on the right.' At which street do you turn? Write the number.
guidedPractice.hint: Second = kedua. Don't turn at the first street.

guidedPractice.prompt: You hear: 'First take a number. Then wait here, please.' What do you do first? Answer in English or Indonesian.
You hear: 'Two tickets to Bogor, please.' — 'That's six thousand rupiah. The train leaves from platform three.' Where are they? Write the place in English.
guidedPractice.hint: Ticket, train, platform: what place has all of these?

independentPractice.prompt: You hear: 'The bus to Malang is delayed by fifteen minutes.' How long is the delay? Write the number of minutes.
independentPractice.hint: fifTEEN has the stress at the end; FIFty at the start.

independentPractice.prompt: You hear: 'The pharmacy is opposite the bank.' Where is the pharmacy? Answer in Indonesian.
You hear: 'Is this the bus to Blok M?' — 'No, this bus goes to Kota. Take bus number six.' Is the first bus the correct bus for Blok M? Write yes or no.
independentPractice.hint: Listen to the first word of the answer.

assessment.prompt: Listen to the announcement. Which gate do passengers for Bali go to? Write the number.
assessment.listen: Attention, please. Flight G A four oh four to Bali is now boarding at gate thirteen. Passengers for Bali, please go to gate thirteen.
assessment.rubric: Correct: 13. 30 = 0 (thirty has the stress at the start; thirTEEN at the end). 404 = 0 (that's the flight number, not the gate).

assessment.prompt: Listen to the announcement. Which platform does the train to Bandung leave from now? Write the number.
assessment.listen: Attention, please. The train to Bandung now leaves from platform six, not platform two. Passengers for Bandung, please go to platform six.
assessment.rubric: Correct: 6. 2 = 0 (that's the old platform: 'not platform two').

assessment.prompt: Listen to the announcement. What time does the train to Surabaya leave now? Write the time in numbers, like 6:00.
assessment.listen: Good morning, passengers. The eight forty-five train to Surabaya is delayed by thirty minutes. It now leaves at nine fifteen from platform four.
assessment.rubric: Correct: 9:15. 8:45 = 0 (the old time, before the delay). 30 or 9:30 = 0 (thirty minutes is how long the delay is). 4 = 0 (the platform).

assessment.prompt: Listen to the directions to the post office. At the second street, do you turn left or right? Write one word in English.
assessment.listen: Sari: Excuse me, where's the post office? Man: Go straight on and take the second street on the left. The post office is on the right, next to a café.
assessment.rubric: Correct: left. 'right' = 0 (on the right is where the post office is, not where you turn).

assessment.prompt: Listen to the pharmacist. How many times a day do you take the tablet? Write the number.
assessment.listen: Take one tablet three times a day, after you eat. Drink a lot of water, and don't drive after you take it.
assessment.rubric: Correct: 3 (three times a day). 1 = 0 (one is how many tablets each time, not how many times a day).

assessment.prompt: Listen to the conversation. Where are Budi and the woman? Write the place in English.
assessment.listen: Woman: Good evening. A table for two? Budi: Yes, please. Woman: Here's the menu. Budi: Thanks. Two iced teas and two plates of fried rice, please.
assessment.rubric: Correct: a restaurant (a café is also fine: a table, a menu, ordering food and drinks). A shop, a hotel or a station = 0.

assessment.prompt: Listen to Rina and Budi. What day do they meet? Write the day in English.
assessment.listen: Rina: Budi, can we meet on Thursday? Budi: Sorry, I can't. I'm busy on Thursday. Is Friday OK? Rina: Yes, Friday is fine. See you then!
assessment.rubric: Correct: Friday. Thursday = 0 (Budi is busy on Thursday, so they change the day). 'Jumat' (in Indonesian) = 50.

blocks.text:
Real announcements and conversations don't wait for you. Four habits help:
- **Read the question first.** It tells you what to listen for: *Which gate?* → a number, *What time?* → a time, *Left or right?* → a direction, *Where are they?* → a place.
- **Listen for the key word**, not every word. In announcements the key information comes right after words like *The train to…*, *gate*, *platform*, *at* and *by*.
- **Don't panic** when you hear a word you don't know. Keep listening: the next words often have the information you need.
- **Listen twice:** first for the general idea, then for the detail.

Missed it in real life? Say **Sorry, can you say that again?**

id.text:
Pengumuman dan percakapan sungguhan tidak menunggumu. Empat kebiasaan ini membantu:
- **Baca pertanyaannya dulu.** Pertanyaan memberitahu apa yang harus kamu dengarkan: *Which gate?* → angka, *What time?* → jam, *Left or right?* → arah, *Where are they?* → tempat.
- **Dengarkan kata kuncinya**, bukan setiap kata. Di pengumuman, info kuncinya ada tepat setelah kata seperti *The train to…*, *gate*, *platform*, *at* dan *by*.
- **Jangan panik** kalau mendengar kata yang tidak kamu tahu. Terus dengarkan: kata-kata berikutnya sering berisi info yang kamu perlukan.
- **Dengarkan dua kali:** pertama untuk gambaran umumnya, lalu untuk detailnya.

Tidak tertangkap di dunia nyata? Bilang **Sorry, can you say that again?** (Maaf, bisa diulang?)

blocks.text: A common Indonesian habit: translating every word in your head. While you translate one word, the speaker says the next sentence and you miss the gate number! Don't stop at a new word like *passengers* (penumpang). Let it go and wait for the number, the place or the time.

id.text: Kebiasaan yang sering terjadi: menerjemahkan setiap kata di kepala. Saat kamu menerjemahkan satu kata, pembicaranya sudah mengucapkan kalimat berikutnya dan kamu kehilangan nomor gate-nya! Jangan berhenti di kata baru seperti *passengers* (penumpang). Biarkan saja, lalu tunggu angka, tempat atau jamnya.

blocks.prompt: The question is 'How long is the delay?'. What do you listen for?
blocks.explain: How long asks for an amount of time, so listen for minutes, usually right after 'delayed by': delayed by twenty minutes.

id.prompt: Pertanyaannya 'How long is the delay?' (Berapa lama keterlambatannya?). Apa yang perlu kamu dengarkan?
id.explain: How long menanyakan lamanya waktu, jadi dengarkan jumlah menit, biasanya tepat setelah 'delayed by': delayed by twenty minutes (terlambat dua puluh menit).

blocks.text:
Most announcements follow the same pattern:
- **Attention, please.** or **Good morning, passengers.** = an announcement starts.
- **What:** *Flight GA 404 to Bali…*, *The train to Bandung…*. The city comes right after **to**.
- **The key facts:** **gate** or **platform** + a number, a **time**, and the news.

The news uses **fixed phrases** (ungkapan tetap). Learn them as whole chunks:
- **is now boarding at gate 7** = passengers get on the plane now at gate 7
- **leaves from platform 3** = the train goes from platform 3
- **is delayed by 30 minutes** = it's 30 minutes late (*by* + how long)
- **now leaves at 9:15** = the new time
- **is cancelled** = it doesn't go today
- **final call** = the last announcement: go to the gate now!

**Flight numbers** are said one digit at a time, and 0 is often said **oh**: *GA 404* = 'G A four oh four'.

id.text:
Kebanyakan pengumuman punya pola yang sama:
- **Attention, please.** atau **Good morning, passengers.** = pengumuman dimulai.
- **Apa yang diumumkan:** *Flight GA 404 to Bali…* (penerbangan GA 404 ke Bali), *The train to Bandung…* (kereta ke Bandung). Nama kotanya ada tepat setelah **to**.
- **Info kunci:** **gate** (pintu keberangkatan) atau **platform** (peron) + nomor, **jam**, dan kabarnya.

Kabarnya memakai **ungkapan tetap** (fixed phrases). Hafalkan sebagai satu kesatuan:
- **is now boarding at gate 7** = penumpang sekarang naik pesawat di gate 7
- **leaves from platform 3** = kereta berangkat dari peron 3
- **is delayed by 30 minutes** = terlambat 30 menit (*by* + berapa lama)
- **now leaves at 9:15** = sekarang berangkat pukul 9.15 (jam yang baru)
- **is cancelled** = dibatalkan, tidak berangkat hari ini
- **final call** = panggilan terakhir: segera ke gate sekarang!

**Nomor penerbangan** dibaca satu angka demi satu angka, dan 0 sering dibaca **oh**: *GA 404* = 'G A four oh four'.

rows.en: Attention, please. Flight GA 404 to Bali is now boarding at gate 7.
rows.id: Mohon perhatian. Penumpang penerbangan GA 404 ke Bali sekarang naik pesawat di gate 7.

id.note: GA 404 dibaca 'G A four oh four'

rows.en: The train to Bandung leaves from platform 3 at 10:20.
rows.id: Kereta ke Bandung berangkat dari peron 3 pukul 10.20.
rows.note: the city after 'to', the number after 'platform', the time after 'at'

id.note: kota setelah 'to', nomor setelah 'platform', jam setelah 'at'

rows.en: The train to Surabaya is delayed by 20 minutes. It now leaves at 7:50.
rows.id: Kereta ke Surabaya terlambat 20 menit. Sekarang berangkat pukul 7.50.
rows.note: two numbers: 'by' + how long, 'now' + the new time

id.note: dua angka: 'by' + berapa lama, 'now' + jam yang baru

rows.en: The bus to Malang is cancelled.
This is the final call for flight GA 218 to Medan.
rows.id: Ini panggilan terakhir untuk penerbangan GA 218 ke Medan.

blocks.text: Careful with **thirTEEN / THIRty** and **fifTEEN / FIFty**: gate 13 and gate 30 can be far apart! A -teen number has the stress (the louder part) at the end. And when a train or a plane **is delayed**, you often hear two times: the old one and the new one. The new time comes after **now**. In the USA a platform is often called a **track**.

id.text: Hati-hati dengan **thirTEEN / THIRty** dan **fifTEEN / FIFty**: gate 13 dan gate 30 bisa berjauhan! Angka -teen tekanannya (bagian yang lebih keras) di akhir. Lalu, kalau kereta atau pesawat **is delayed** (terlambat), kamu sering mendengar dua jam: jam yang lama dan jam yang baru. Jam yang baru ada setelah **now**. Di Amerika, peron sering disebut **track**.

blocks.prompt: You hear: 'The train to Bandung is delayed by twenty minutes. It now leaves at ten forty.' When does the train leave?
blocks.explain: The new time comes after 'now': ten forty = 10:40. Twenty is how long the delay is.

id.prompt: Kamu mendengar: 'The train to Bandung is delayed by twenty minutes. It now leaves at ten forty.' Jam berapa keretanya berangkat?
id.explain: Jam yang baru ada setelah 'now': ten forty = 10.40. Twenty (dua puluh) adalah lamanya keterlambatan.

blocks.text:
You know **turn left**, **turn right** and **go straight on**. Real directions add a few chunks:
- **take the second street on the left** = turn left at street number 2 (don't turn at the first street!)
- **go past the bank** = don't stop and don't turn at the bank
- **opposite the mosque** = across the road from the mosque
- **at the end of the street** = where the street stops
- **cross the road** = go to the other side

**Instructions** tell you how to do something. Like directions, they start with the **verb** (the action word): *Press…*, *Take…*, *Wait…*. Listen for the order words **first**, **then** and **after that**, and for **don't** (= do not).

id.text:
Kamu sudah tahu **turn left** (belok kiri), **turn right** (belok kanan) dan **go straight on** (jalan lurus). Petunjuk arah sungguhan menambah beberapa ungkapan:
- **take the second street on the left** = belok kiri di jalan nomor 2 (jangan belok di jalan pertama!)
- **go past the bank** = lewati bank-nya, jangan berhenti dan jangan belok di sana
- **opposite the mosque** = di seberang masjid
- **at the end of the street** = di ujung jalan
- **cross the road** = seberangi jalan

**Instruksi** memberitahu cara melakukan sesuatu. Seperti petunjuk arah, kalimatnya diawali **kata kerja** (kata yang menunjukkan tindakan): *Press…* (tekan), *Take…* (ambil), *Wait…* (tunggu). Dengarkan kata urutan **first** (pertama/dulu), **then** (lalu) dan **after that** (setelah itu), dan juga **don't** (jangan).

rows.en: Go straight on, past the school.
Take the second street on the left.
The ATM is opposite the mosque.

id.note: bahasa Inggris Amerika sering bilang 'across from'

rows.en: First press the green button. Then take your ticket.
rows.id: Tekan tombol hijau dulu. Lalu ambil tiketmu.

blocks.text: Two Indonesian traps. **Second** here means *kedua* (number 2), not *detik*. And **take** in *take the second street* doesn't mean *ambil*: it means you go into that street. Also remember from A1: **turn left** is what you do, **on the left** is where the place is. British English says *go straight on* and *opposite*; Americans often say *go straight ahead* and *across from*.

id.text: Dua jebakan untuk penutur bahasa Indonesia. **Second** di sini artinya *kedua* (nomor 2), bukan *detik*. Dan **take** di *take the second street* bukan *ambil*: artinya kamu masuk ke jalan itu. Ingat juga dari A1: **turn left** adalah yang kamu lakukan (belok kiri), **on the left** adalah letak tempatnya (di sebelah kiri). Bahasa Inggris Britania bilang *go straight on* dan *opposite*; orang Amerika sering bilang *go straight ahead* dan *across from*.

blocks.prompt: You hear: 'Take the third street on the right.' What do you do?
options: Turn left at the third street.
Turn right at the third street.
Turn right at the first street.
blocks.explain: Third = ketiga, so you count three streets, and 'on the right' tells you to turn right there.

id.prompt: Kamu mendengar: 'Take the third street on the right.' Apa yang kamu lakukan?
id.explain: Third = ketiga, jadi kamu hitung tiga jalan, dan 'on the right' berarti kamu belok kanan di sana.

material.title: The main point of a conversation

blocks.text:
The **main point** is the most important idea, not every detail. Ask yourself three questions:
- **Where are they?** Listen for place words: *menu, table* → a restaurant; *ticket, platform* → a station; *appointment, doctor* → a clinic.
- **What does someone want, or what is the problem?** Listen after **but**, **sorry** and **I can't**.
- **What do they decide?** The answer is often at the **end**, after *OK*, *fine* or *great*.

Small words like *um*, *well* or *oh* don't carry information. Don't worry about them.

id.text:
**Poin utama** (main point) adalah ide yang paling penting, bukan setiap detail. Tanyakan tiga hal pada dirimu:
- **Mereka di mana?** Dengarkan kata tempat: *menu, table* (meja) → restoran; *ticket, platform* → stasiun; *appointment* (janji temu), *doctor* → klinik.
- **Apa yang diinginkan seseorang, atau apa masalahnya?** Dengarkan setelah **but** (tapi), **sorry** (maaf) dan **I can't** (aku tidak bisa).
- **Apa keputusan mereka?** Jawabannya sering ada di **akhir**, setelah *OK*, *fine* (bisa/baik) atau *great* (bagus).

Kata kecil seperti *um*, *well* atau *oh* tidak membawa info. Tidak usah dipikirkan.

rows.en: Sorry, I can't. I'm busy on Monday.
rows.id: Maaf, aku tidak bisa. Aku sibuk hari Senin.

rows.note: the decision: often at the end

rows.en: Is this the bus to Bogor? — No, it isn't. That bus is over there.
rows.id: Ini bus ke Bogor? — Bukan. Busnya di sebelah sana.

blocks.text: In Indonesian, a polite 'no' is often soft (*wah, kayaknya nggak bisa…*). English is soft too: **Sorry, I can't** or **I'm busy then** means *no*. Then the speaker often gives a new idea: **What about…?** or **Is … OK?** (Bagaimana kalau…?). So the first plan is often not the final plan: listen to the end.

id.text: Dalam bahasa Indonesia, 'tidak' yang sopan sering diucapkan halus (*wah, kayaknya nggak bisa…*). Bahasa Inggris juga halus: **Sorry, I can't** atau **I'm busy then** artinya *tidak bisa*. Lalu pembicara sering memberi usul baru: **What about…?** atau **Is … OK?** (Bagaimana kalau…?). Jadi rencana pertama sering bukan rencana akhirnya: dengarkan sampai selesai.

blocks.prompt: You hear: 'Good morning. I have an appointment with Doctor Hasan at ten.' — 'OK. Please sit down and wait. He is with a patient now.' Where are they?
blocks.explain: Appointment, doctor and patient (pasien) are clinic words, so they are at a clinic.

id.prompt: Kamu mendengar: 'Good morning. I have an appointment with Doctor Hasan at ten.' — 'OK. Please sit down and wait. He is with a patient now.' Mereka di mana?
id.explain: Appointment (janji temu), doctor dan patient (pasien) adalah kata-kata di klinik, jadi mereka ada di klinik.

suggestedQuestions: Why is 0 said 'oh' in flight numbers?
What's the difference between 'is delayed' and 'is cancelled'?
What does 'take the second street on the left' mean?
How can I find the main point when I don't understand every word?

resources.title: Transport announcements
resources.note: A2 listening: four real-style announcements at a train station, an airport gate and the London Underground (a platform change, a delay). With transcript and exercises.

id.note: Menyimak A2: empat pengumuman seperti aslinya di stasiun kereta, gate bandara dan kereta bawah tanah London (pindah peron, keterlambatan). Ada transkrip dan latihannya.

resources.title: Four conversations
resources.note: A2 listening: four short everyday conversations; you match each one to its main topic. Some sentences use the past tense, which comes in a later lesson.

id.note: Menyimak A2: empat percakapan pendek sehari-hari; kamu mencocokkan tiap percakapan dengan topik utamanya. Beberapa kalimat memakai bentuk lampau, yang dipelajari di pelajaran berikutnya.

id.intro: Selamat datang! Di pelajaran ini kamu melatih telinga untuk situasi nyata: pengumuman di bandara dan stasiun, petunjuk arah dan instruksi sederhana, dan percakapan pendek. Kamu tidak perlu menangkap setiap kata: baca dulu pertanyaannya, dengarkan info kuncinya, dan tetap tenang kalau mendengar kata yang tidak kamu tahu.
suggestedQuestions: Apa arti 'take the second street on the left'?
Bagaimana cara menangkap poin utama kalau aku tidak mengerti setiap kata?

assessment.lp-1: Dengarkan pengumumannya. Penumpang ke Bali harus pergi ke gate nomor berapa? Tulis nomornya.
assessment.lp-2: Dengarkan pengumumannya. Sekarang kereta ke Bandung berangkat dari peron (platform) nomor berapa? Tulis nomornya.
assessment.lp-3: Dengarkan pengumumannya. Sekarang kereta ke Surabaya berangkat jam berapa? Tulis jamnya dengan angka, seperti 6:00.
assessment.lp-4: Dengarkan petunjuk arah ke kantor pos. Di jalan kedua, kamu belok kiri atau kanan? Tulis satu kata dalam bahasa Inggris.
assessment.lp-5: Dengarkan apoteker itu. Berapa kali sehari kamu minum tabletnya? Tulis angkanya.
assessment.lp-6: Dengarkan percakapannya. Budi dan perempuan itu ada di mana? Tulis tempatnya dalam bahasa Inggris.
assessment.lp-7: Dengarkan Rina dan Budi. Mereka bertemu hari apa? Tulis harinya dalam bahasa Inggris.
